messages:
Amy Chen: FYI customer reported being billed for ~600 extra tokens after a reconnect during a streaming + toolcall flow. They say client disconnected right after toolcall start.
Ravi Patel: ugh. Do we have reproducible steps? streaming reconnect often double-counts if we treat preemptive toolcall payloads as committed.
Amy Chen: I reproduced locally by interrupting the socket during a toolcall request. They got charged for the toolcall response even though the client never received it.
Ben Ortiz: that's the classic 'preemptive commit' problem. Server generates tokens -> caches them -> route dies -> client reconnects -> we re-stream or re-run -> billing duplicates.
Kate Li: from billing POV we have two options: 1) bill on "generated" tokens (current) 2) bill on "delivered/acked" tokens and hold provisional credits. Option 2 requires reconcilers and more telemetry but is fairer.
Lucy Morales: for product / console UX we need to show provisional vs final tokens on each request in the console. Users get very upset seeing a spike that later disappears with no explanation.
Ravi Patel: could we implement a provisional charge ID that is annotated on the request and reconciled after a short window (like 30s)? If client reconnects and resumes, we mark as final; if not, we refund provisional.
Kate Li: yes but refunds are messy. Better: show "provisional" line items and don't invoice until finalized. For Hosted free credit use-case, provisional may still consume quota until finalized; we should surface that.
Ben Ortiz: technically we can mark tokens as provisional in the token-accounting stream and emit a finalization event. Pseudocode:
```
emit_charge(request_id, tokens, provisional=true)
// later:
emit_finalize(request_id, tokens_final)
```
Indexing the provisional ID in billing tables lets us avoid double invoices.
Amy Chen: edge case: toolcalls that get truncated by the client (client sends cancel mid-toolcall). The model may have produced N tokens but truncation means the tool saw only M. Which tokens do we charge?
Ravi Patel: I think we should bill for what the model produced server-side, unless the tool never executed due to truncation. But in streaming it's fuzzy.
Kate Li: we need deterministic rules: - streaming main/assistant tokens: bill on finalization - toolcall invocation tokens (prompt + tool request): bill immediately - toolcall response tokens: bill on delivery to client or tool execution success. Document this.
Lucy Morales: can we add a console flag that shows "billing state" on each call: provisional / finalized / refunded and a short reason? e.g., "reconnect before ACK", "client-cancel", "tool-failed".
Ben Ortiz: yes. Also add telemetry metrics: provisional_count, finalize_latency, provisional_refund_rate. That will help us tune the timeout and show health.
Amy Chen: a few implementation notes: 1) router needs to propagate charge_id through reconnects 2) cache eviction must not orphan provisional IDs 3) edge case: cross-path retries where different backend handles retry — charge_id must be client-visible.
Ravi Patel: agree. For reconnect flow: attach header `X-Charge-ID: <uuid>` on the socket handshake and persist in session storage so retries reuse it.
Amy Chen: sample header idea in logs: `X-Charge-ID: a1b2c3d4` — we should show this in debug mode in the console.
Kate Li: sounds good. Also add billing reconciliation job that waits 24h and then auto-refunds if finalize never arrives. But set alerting before refunds.
ingest-bot: incident created: #INC-2026-119 - customer complaint: double charge on streaming toolcall. Assigned: Amy Chen, Kate Li.
Lucy Morales: UX ask: small tooltip on per-request row: "Provisional charges may change after finalization. Click for reconciliation history." Should be in next sprint.
Ravi Patel: next steps for eng: (1) implement provisional charge events and `X-Charge-ID` propagation (2) add finalize/timeout pipeline (3) emit telemetry metrics (4) expose provisional/final in console. I'll open RFC PR.
Amy Chen: thanks. I'll add the reproduction steps and small reproducible harness to the RFC. Anyone object to 30s provisional window as starting point?
Kate Li: start with 30s, monitor finalize latency metric; require product signoff before changing billing behavior.
Ben Ortiz: no objections. :thumbsup:
Amy Chen: cool. I'll follow up with the RFC link and a short demo video.
